l: mankind, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Mankind is addressed with revelation, warnings, promises, and similitudes. People are told that whoever goes right benefits the soul, while whoever strays harms only the soul.

l: false gods, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: False gods are rejected because they have no power or intelligence and cannot remove hurt or restrain mercy. Those who put them away and turn to Allah in repentance receive glad tidings.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The Hereafter brings greater doom for those who reject Allah and reward for those who keep their duty to Him. People return to their Lord and are informed of what they did.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: On the Day of Resurrection, people dispute before their Lord, faces of those who lied concerning Allah are blackened, and each soul is paid in full for what it did.

l: the Fire, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The Fire is the fate of those who reject Allah and His revelations. It has an awning above and a dais beneath, and people are warned to fear it.

l: hell, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Hell receives disbelievers in troops after its gates are opened. They enter it to dwell therein, and it is called the hapless journey's end of the scorners.

l: the Garden, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The Garden receives those who keep their duty to Allah in troops. Its gates are opened to them with peace, and they dwell therein as a reward for their works.

l: doom, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Doom comes upon those who deny, scorn, and do wrong, sometimes from where they do not know. People are warned to repent and follow revelation before doom comes suddenly.

l: mercy, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Allah's mercy is offered to those who have been prodigal to their own hurt, and they are told not to despair. Those who hope for their Lord's mercy are contrasted with disbelievers.

l: guidance, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Guidance comes from Allah through revelation and remembrance. Those whom Allah guides cannot be misled, while those whom Allah sends astray have no guide.

l: the heavens, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth, and the heavens belong to Him. On the Day of Resurrection, the heavens are rolled in His right hand.

l: the earth, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Allah created the earth, sends water into it, and brings forth crops of diverse hues that later wither and become chaff. On the Day of Resurrection, the earth shines with the light of its Lord.

l: human beings, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Human beings are created from one being, and Allah provides for them and creates them in their mothers' wombs. They receive warnings, guidance, and judgment according to what they do.

l: the soul, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The soul is received by Allah at death and during sleep. Allah keeps the soul for which He has ordained death and releases the others until an appointed term.

l: the day, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The day succeeds the night by Allah's command, and the night succeeds the day. The text also warns of a tremendous Day and the coming Day of Resurrection.

l: death, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Death comes to Muhammad and to all others. Allah receives the souls at death and determines their appointed terms.

l: the trumpet, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The trumpet is blown, causing those in the heavens and the earth to swoon except whom Allah wills. It is blown a second time, and they stand waiting.

l: the angels, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The angels throng around the Throne, hymning the praises of their Lord. They are present when judgment is completed aright.

l: the truth, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The truth is revealed in the Scripture and is brought by those who believe in it. Those who deny the truth when it reaches them are called wrongdoers and face hell.

l: repentance, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Repentance involves turning to Allah, putting away false gods, and surrendering to Him before doom arrives. Those who repent are given glad tidings.

l: thankfulness, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Allah is pleased with thankfulness, and people are commanded to serve Him and be among the thankful. Thankfulness is contrasted with thanklessness, which Allah does not approve for His bondmen.

l: disbelief, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Disbelief brings warning, humiliation, loss, and the Fire. Muhammad is told to let disbelievers take pleasure briefly because they are among the owners of the Fire.

l: the promise of Allah, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: The promise of Allah is that those who keep their duty to Him will receive lofty halls with rivers flowing beneath them. Allah does not fail His promise, and the people of the Garden praise Him for fulfilling it.

l: Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: This unit concerns Allah, Muhammad, Moses, Pharaoh, Pharaoh's family, the messengers, the angels bearing the Throne, the believers, and the disbelievers. It describes Allah as the Forgiver, the Accepter of repentance, the Stern in punishment, and the Creator and Lord of all things. Moses brings revelations and clear proofs to Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah, while a believing man of Pharaoh's family warns his people and Pharaoh's plot ends in ruin. The unit warns of the Hour, describes the fate of the disbelievers in the Fire, and promises guidance, forgiveness, and the Gardens of Eden to believers who do right.

l: Allah, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Allah is the Mighty, the Knower, the Forgiver of sin, the Accepter of repentance, the Stern in punishment, and the Bountiful. Allah shows signs, sends provision, judges with truth, guides whom He wills, gives life and death, and hears prayer. Allah helps the messengers and believers, wards off evils from them, and punishes disbelievers and wrong-doers.

l: Muhammad, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Muhammad is warned of the Day of Meeting, the approaching doom, and the Day of Summoning. He is told to have patience, ask forgiveness, praise Allah, and call people to worship Allah alone.

l: Moses, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Moses is sent with Allah's revelations and a clear warrant to Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah. Pharaoh seeks to kill Moses, but Moses seeks refuge in Allah from every scorner who does not believe in a Day of Reckoning.

l: Pharaoh, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Pharaoh calls Moses a lying sorcerer and orders the sons of those who believe with him to be slain. He seeks to kill Moses, asks Haman to build a tower, and is debarred from the right way; Pharaoh's plot ends in ruin.

l: the messengers, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The messengers bring clear proofs from Allah, but many people disbelieve, argue falsely, or mock what they bring. Allah helps His messengers and those who believe in the life of the world and on the day when the witnesses arise.

l: the angels bearing the Throne, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The angels bearing the Throne and those around it hymn the praises of their Lord, believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe. They ask Allah to forgive believers who repent and follow His way and to admit them and their righteous fathers, wives, and descendants into the Gardens of Eden.

l: the believers, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The believers are prayed for by the angels bearing the Throne. Allah wards off ill-deeds from them, helps them in the life of the world and on the day when the witnesses arise, and promises them forgiveness and the Gardens of Eden.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The disbelievers argue about Allah's revelations without warrant, reject the messengers and the Scripture, and ascribe partners to Allah. They are informed of Allah's abhorrence, dragged through boiling waters, thrust into the Fire, and ultimately ruined.

l: Pharaoh's family, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Pharaoh's family is encompassed by a dreadful doom. They are exposed to the Fire morning and evening, and when the Hour arises they are commanded to enter the most awful doom.

l: the believing man of Pharaoh's family, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The believing man of Pharaoh's family hides his faith and argues against killing a man who says that his Lord is Allah. He warns his people about the fate of earlier peoples and the Day of Summoning, and he says that he entrusts his cause to Allah.

l: the earth, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The earth is made a dwelling-place for people. Allah has appointed signs in it, and earlier peoples left traces in it, though their power and what they earned did not save them.

l: the heavens, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. The heavens are among the roads that Pharaoh hopes to reach so that he may look upon the god of Moses.

l: the sky, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Allah appoints the sky as a canopy and sends down provision from it.

l: the Fire, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The Fire is the abode of disbelievers and the destination of those who call others to disbelief and association with Allah. Its inhabitants are dragged through boiling waters, thrust into it, and ask its guards for relief, but the prayer of disbelievers is in vain.

l: the Gardens of Eden, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The Gardens of Eden are promised to believers who repent and follow Allah's way. The angels ask Allah to admit believers and their righteous fathers, wives, and descendants into them, where they will be nourished without stint.

l: the world, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The life of the world is described as a passing comfort. In the world, Allah helps His messengers and believers, provides signs and good things, and warns people of the consequences faced by earlier nations.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The Hereafter is the enduring home. In it, every soul is requited for what it earned, and the disbelievers and wrong-doers face the Fire and the ill abode.

l: the Scripture, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The Scripture is revealed from Allah, and those who deny it will come to know the consequence. Allah causes the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture as a guide and reminder for men of understanding.

l: the revelations of Allah, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The revelations of Allah are disputed by disbelievers and arrogant people without warrant. Those who deny them are turned away, while they serve as clear signs of Allah's Sovereignty.

l: the clear proofs, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The clear proofs are brought by the messengers, including Moses, but disbelievers reject them. The believing man of Pharaoh's family asks whether a man should be killed because he brings clear proofs from his Lord.

l: the Truth, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Moses brings the Truth from Allah's presence, but Pharaoh and his people reject it and plot against those who believe with him.

l: religion, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Religion is to be made pure for Allah alone, however much the disbelievers are averse. Pharaoh claims to fear that Moses will alter the people's religion.

l: faith, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Faith in Allah is refused by the disbelievers when they are called to it, but the believers follow Allah's way. The believing man of Pharaoh's family hides his faith, and the disbelievers' faith cannot benefit them when they see Allah's doom.

l: disbelief, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Disbelief includes rejecting Allah when He alone is invoked, while believing when a partner is ascribed to Him. Disbelief leads its people to argument, punishment, the Fire, and ruin.

l: repentance, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Allah is the Accepter of repentance. Those who repent and follow His way are included in the angels' prayer for forgiveness and protection from the punishment of hell.

l: sin, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Allah is the Forgiver of sin. Earlier peoples are seized for their sins, and every soul is requited for what it has earned.

l: forgiveness, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Forgiveness is sought for those who believe, repent, and follow Allah's way. Muhammad is instructed to ask forgiveness of his sin.

l: punishment, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Allah is Stern in punishment and severe in punishment. Punishment comes upon disbelieving peoples, encompasses Pharaoh's family, and includes the Fire and the most awful doom.

l: the Hour, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The Hour is surely coming, with no doubt about it, though most people do not believe. When it arises, Pharaoh's family is ordered to enter the most awful doom.

l: the day of judgment, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: On the day of judgment, each soul is requited for what it earned and no wrong is done. The witnesses arise, excuses do not benefit the evil-doers, and the disbelievers are brought to punishment.

l: the revelation of the Scripture, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The revelation of the Scripture is from Allah, the Mighty, the Knower. It establishes Allah's authority and calls people toward worship of Him alone.

l: the resurrection, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: The unit describes people being brought forth, gathered, and judged after death. It also describes the day when the dead are raised and the witnesses arise, though the term resurrection is not used in the text.

l: prayer, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Allah commands people to pray to Him with religion pure for Him alone and promises to hear their prayer. The prayer of disbelievers is declared to be in vain.

l: guidance, Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir), Surah 40: The Forgiver (Al-Ghaafir)
s: Allah gives guidance, and Moses is given guidance before the Children of Israel inherit the Scripture as a guide and reminder. Whoever Allah sends astray has no guide, while the believing man of Pharaoh's family calls his people to the way of right conduct.

l: Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: This unit concerns Allah's revelation to Muhammad, presented as an Arabic Lecture and Scripture explaining the truth, warning disbelievers, and giving good tidings to believers. It recounts the creation of the earth and heavens, the destruction of A'ad and Thamud, and the future judgment of humankind, including testimony by their own bodies and punishment in the Fire. It teaches that Allah is One, that the straight path requires worship, uprightness, repentance, and good deeds, and that evil should be repelled with what is better. It also declares that the revelation is secure from falsehood and that Allah's signs will be shown on the horizons and within people until the truth becomes clear.

l: Allah, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Allah is described as One, the Lord of the Worlds, the Creator, the Forgiving and Merciful, the Hearer and Knower, and the Able to do all things. He created the earth and heavens, knows all things including the Hour and human births, witnesses everything, and will judge people fairly without wronging His slaves.

l: Muhammad, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Muhammad is told to say that he is only a mortal like others, but that it is inspired to him that Allah is One. He is instructed to call people to the straight path, seek Allah's forgiveness, warn them, and respond to evil with what is better.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The Qur'an is rejected by those who disbelieve, who tell others not to heed it and to drown out its hearing. It is described as an unassailable revelation that falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it.

l: the Scripture, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The Scripture is a revelation from the Beneficent and Merciful in which the verses are expounded. It is presented in Arabic for people who have knowledge and contains good tidings and warning.

l: the revelation, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The revelation comes from Allah and is described as wise, praiseworthy, and protected from falsehood. It gives guidance and healing to those who believe, while disbelievers experience deafness and blindness toward it.

l: the Reminder, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The Reminder is rejected by those who disbelieve when it comes to them. It is described as an unassailable Scripture that falsehood cannot approach.

l: the Lecture in Arabic, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The Lecture in Arabic has verses that are expounded for people who have knowledge. If it had been in a foreign tongue, people would have objected that its verses were not explained, but for believers it is guidance and healing.

l: the idolaters, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The idolaters are warned because they give not the poor-due, disbelieve in the Hereafter, and ascribe rivals to Allah. They are called to take the straight path and seek forgiveness.

l: the believers, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The believers who do good works receive an enduring reward. Those who say that their Lord is Allah and remain upright receive the descent of angels with reassurance, good tidings, protection, and whatever their souls desire.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The disbelievers turn away from the message, reject Allah's revelations, and try to prevent others from hearing the Qur'an. They will taste an awful doom, be requited for their deeds, and acknowledge on the Day of Resurrection that their supposed partners were not witnesses for them.

l: the angels, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The angels descend upon those who say that Allah is their Lord and remain upright, telling them not to fear or grieve and giving them good tidings of Paradise. They are also described as protecting friends in the life of the world and in the Hereafter, while those with Allah glorify Him continually.

l: the messengers, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The messengers before Muhammad also received statements like those given to him. Their peoples were told to worship none but Allah, but some demanded that angels be sent and became disbelievers.

l: the jinn, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The jinn are included among those who may beguile people. On the Day of Resurrection, disbelievers will ask for those who beguiled them from the jinn and humankind so they can place them beneath their feet.

l: humankind, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Humankind is warned, tested, and judged according to its deeds. People may become arrogant, despair when harmed, withdraw when shown favour, and wrongly assume that the Hour will not come, but Allah will show them His signs within themselves and hold them accountable.

l: the enemies of Allah, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The enemies of Allah are gathered and driven toward the Fire. Their ears, eyes, and skins testify against their deeds, and their lasting home is the Fire because they denied Allah's revelations.

l: the earth, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Allah created the earth in two Days, placed firm hills in it, blessed it, and measured its sustenance in four Days. When water is sent upon it, the earth thrills and grows, demonstrating Allah's power to bring the dead to life.

l: the heaven, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The heaven was smoke when Allah turned to it and to the earth, and both came willingly or unwillingly in obedience. Allah ordained the heavens as seven heavens in two Days, inspired each with its mandate, and adorned the nearest heaven with lamps.

l: the Fire, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The Fire is the destination of Allah's enemies and the immortal home of those who denied His revelations. Disbelievers are driven toward it, and they will not be granted favour when they ask for it.

l: Paradise, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Paradise is promised to those who say that Allah is their Lord and remain upright. The angels give them good tidings of it and of whatever their souls desire, as a gift of welcome from One Forgiving and Merciful.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The Hereafter contains greater shame and punishment for those destroyed in the world, while the upright receive protection and blessings there. Disbelievers deny it, but they will be judged and punished according to their deeds.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: On the Day of Resurrection, people will be gathered and disbelievers will be driven toward the Fire. Their ears, eyes, and skins will testify against them, and they will recognize that their supposed partners were not witnesses for them.

l: the Hour, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Knowledge of the Hour belongs to Allah. People doubt that it will occur, but if they are returned to their Lord, Allah will tell the disbelievers what they did and make them taste hard punishment.

l: the creation of the earth and heavens, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Allah created the earth in two Days, placed and supplied it, then ordained the seven heavens in two Days. He created the earth and heavens with power and knowledge, and the creation shows His measuring and authority.

l: the doom of the Hereafter, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The doom of the Hereafter is more shameful than the punishment of the worldly life. Those who deny Allah's revelations will taste an awful and hard punishment and will not be helped.

l: guidance, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Guidance is given by Allah, but Thamud preferred blindness to it. The revelation is guidance and healing for those who believe, while those who reject it are described as deaf and blind.

l: the straight path, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Muhammad is instructed to call people to take the straight path unto Allah and seek His forgiveness. The path is connected with affirming Allah's oneness and turning away from idolatry.

l: good deeds, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Good deeds are rewarded by Allah, and those who believe and do good works receive an enduring reward. A good deed should be used to repel an evil deed, potentially turning enmity into intimate friendship.

l: evil deeds, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: Evil deeds are not equal to good deeds and are held against the person who commits them. They are to be repelled with what is better, and those who do wrong will face Allah's judgment.

l: the truth, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: The revelation is the truth, and Allah will show His portents on the horizons and within people until its truth becomes manifest to them. Those who reject it are described as being in open feud and as further astray.

l: the meeting with their Lord, Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat), Surah 41: Explained in detail (Fussilat)
s: People are warned not to remain in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. The text asks whether Allah is not surrounding all things, indicating that this meeting is within His encompassing knowledge and power.

l: Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: Surah 44 concerns the Scripture revealed by Allah on a blessed night as a warning and mercy, and it calls people to recognize Allah as Lord and reject doubt. It describes the visible smoke, the torment, and the greater seizure awaiting those who turn away, while recounting how Pharaoh's folk opposed the noble messenger and how the Children of Israel were delivered. It contrasts the punishment of the sinner with the secured place prepared for the people of duty on the Day of Decision. Muhammad is told that the Scripture has been made easy in his language and to wait while the disbelievers also wait.

l: Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: Surah 44 concerns the Scripture, the visible smoke, the torment, Pharaoh's folk, the Children of Israel, the Day of Decision, and the contrasting fates of the sinner and the people of duty.

l: Allah, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: Allah is the only deity, gives life and death, and is the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and all between them. He is the Hearer, the Knower, the Mighty, and the Merciful, and He shows mercy to whom He wills.

l: the Scripture, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The Scripture makes the truth plain and was revealed on a blessed night as a warning, a command, and a mercy from Allah. It has been made easy in Muhammad's language so that people may heed.

l: the blessed night, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The blessed night is when the Scripture was revealed and every wise command was made clear.

l: the sky, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The sky will produce visible smoke that will envelop the people.

l: the visible smoke, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The visible smoke will envelop the people and will be a painful torment.

l: the torment, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The torment is painful, and people will ask their Lord to relieve it while claiming belief. The torment will be withdrawn a little, but they will return to disbelief, and a greater seizure will bring punishment.

l: Muhammad, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: Muhammad is told to watch for the day when the sky produces visible smoke and to wait while the disbelievers also wait. The Scripture is made easy in his language so that people may heed.

l: the messenger making plain the Truth, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The messenger making plain the Truth came to the people, but they turned away from him and called him one taught by others and a madman.

l: the Day of the greater seizure, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The Day of the greater seizure is when Allah will seize the people and punish them in truth.

l: Pharaoh, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: Pharaoh was a tyrant of the wanton ones. The Children of Israel were delivered from him and from the shameful doom.

l: Pharaoh's folk, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: Pharaoh's folk were tried when a noble messenger came to them. They were guilty, opposed the messenger, and were ultimately left as a drowned host.

l: the noble messenger to Pharaoh, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The noble messenger asked Pharaoh's folk to give up the slaves of Allah, declared himself faithful, warned them not to be proud against Allah, and brought a clear warrant. He sought refuge in his Lord and their Lord and asked to be allowed to go if they did not believe.

l: the slaves of Allah, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The slaves of Allah were commanded to be taken away by night, and they were followed by Pharaoh's folk.

l: the drowned host, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The drowned host was left behind in the sea after the slaves of Allah were taken away.

l: the Children of Israel, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The Children of Israel were delivered from the shameful doom and from Pharaoh. Allah chose them purposely above all creatures and gave them portents containing a clear trial.

l: the shameful doom, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The shameful doom was imposed on the Children of Israel by Pharaoh, from which Allah delivered them.

l: the resurrection, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: Some people say that there is only their first death and that they will not be raised again. They demand that their fathers be brought back if the claim is true.

l: the Day of Decision, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The Day of Decision is the appointed term for all people. On it, a friend cannot avail a friend, except for one on whom Allah has mercy.

l: the day of judgment, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The day of judgment is described through the Day of Decision, when people are judged and the sinner and the people of duty receive different outcomes.

l: the tree of Zaqqum, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The tree of Zaqqum is the food of the sinner.

l: the sinner, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The sinner will eat from the tree of Zaqqum, which is like molten brass seething in the belly. He will be dragged into the midst of hell and have boiling water poured over his head, and he will be told to taste the punishment.

l: boiling water, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: Boiling water will seethe like molten brass in the sinner's belly and will be poured over his head as torment.

l: hell, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The sinner will be dragged into the midst of hell and punished with boiling water.

l: the people of duty, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The people of duty will be in a secured place amid gardens and watersprings. They will wear silk and silk embroidery, face one another, receive fair ones with wide lovely eyes, call for every fruit in safety, and be saved from the doom of hell.

l: the secured place, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The secured place is where the people of duty will dwell amid gardens and watersprings, safe from the doom of hell.

l: the supreme triumph, Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan), Surah 44: The Smoke (Ad-Dukhaan)
s: The salvation of the people of duty from the doom of hell is called a bounty from Allah and the supreme triumph.

l: Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: This unit concerns Allah’s revelation, the Scripture, and Muhammad’s warning to those who disbelieve and those who believe. It describes Allah’s creation, judgment, forgiveness, punishment, and promise of the Garden, while recounting the destruction of A'ad and the response of the jinn who heard the Qur'an. It commends kindness toward parents and describes the consequences of disbelief, arrogance, and rejection of Allah’s summoner. It ends by instructing Muhammad and the messengers to remain patient until the promised doom comes.

l: Allah, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Allah is described as the source of the revelation and the creator of the heavens and the earth. He knows what people say, forgives, shows mercy, judges deeds, guides whom He wills, and is able to give life to the dead and do all things.

l: Muhammad, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Muhammad is told to warn people, say that he follows only what is inspired in him, and convey Allah’s message. He is instructed to be patient like the stout-hearted messengers and not hasten the doom of those who disbelieve.

l: the Scripture, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The Scripture is revealed by Allah and confirms what was before it. It warns those who do wrong and brings good tidings to the righteous.

l: the revelation, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The revelation is presented as clear signs from Allah and as a warning meant to lead people back. Those who disbelieve call it magic and an ancient lie.

l: the earth, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The earth was created by Allah with truth and for an appointed term. People are challenged to show what their invoked gods created of it.

l: those who disbelieve, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Those who disbelieve turn away from warnings, reject the Truth, and deny Allah’s revelations. They are exposed to the Fire, deprived of the good things they squandered, and rewarded with ignominy and doom.

l: those who believe, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Those who believe are associated with accepting the revelation and following the right path. Those who say that their Lord is Allah and then walk aright will have no fear or grief and will enter the Garden.

l: mankind, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Mankind will be gathered for judgment, when those worshipped besides Allah will become enemies of their worshippers and deny having been worshipped.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The Day of Resurrection is the time until which those invoked besides Allah do not hear the prayers directed to them. It is also when mankind is gathered and those false objects of worship become enemies and deniers.

l: the Truth, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The Truth reaches those who disbelieve through Allah’s clear revelations. They respond by calling it mere magic.

l: Moses, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Moses is connected with the Scripture that existed before the Qur'an. That Scripture is described as an example and a mercy, and the jinn say that the Qur'an confirms what was before it.

l: the Garden, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The Garden is promised to those who walk aright and to those whose best deeds Allah accepts and whose evil deeds He overlooks. They remain immortal there as a reward for what they did.

l: the Fire, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire and asked whether it is real. They affirm that it is real, and are told to taste the doom because they disbelieved.

l: A'ad, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: A'ad is associated with a people warned by the brother of A'ad among the wind-curved sandhills. Their people rejected the warning, and Allah destroyed them with a painful wind.

l: the brother of A'ad, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The brother of A'ad warned his people to serve none but Allah and feared for them the doom of a tremendous Day. His people rejected him and demanded the threatened punishment.

l: the wind-curved sandhills, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The wind-curved sandhills were where the brother of A'ad warned his people. A dense cloud approaching their valleys was revealed to be a destructive wind rather than rain.

l: the wind, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The wind came as a painful torment by command of its Lord and destroyed all things. By morning, nothing could be seen except the dwellings of the guilty people.

l: the jinn, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Certain of the jinn listened to the Qur'an when it was recited and then returned to their people as warners. They said it confirmed what was before it, guided to the truth and a right road, and urged their people to respond to Allah’s summoner.

l: Allah's summoner, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: Allah's summoner calls people to respond to Allah and believe in Him. Those who respond may be forgiven some of their sins and guarded from a painful doom, while those who do not respond cannot escape and have no protecting friends instead of Allah.

l: the messengers, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The messengers include warners who came before and after the brother of A'ad. Muhammad is told to be patient like the stout-hearted among them.

l: the Day of Doom, Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf), Surah 46: The Dunes (Al-Ahqaf)
s: The doom is described as a punishment for disbelief, arrogance, transgression, and rejection of Allah’s warnings. Those who face it will perceive their time in the world as no more than an hour of daylight.

l: Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: This unit contrasts believers who follow Allah's truth with disbelievers who follow falsehood and oppose the way of Allah. Allah promises believers guidance, forgiveness, firm footing, and entry into the Garden, while disbelievers face vain actions, perdition, and the Fire. Muhammad is instructed to know that there is no Allah save Allah, seek forgiveness, obey Allah and the messenger, and remain steadfast in conflict. The unit also discusses battle, war, the Hour, revelation, the Qur'an, and the fleeting nature of the life of the world.

l: Allah, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: Allah renders the actions of disbelievers vain, guides believers, improves their state, and grants them the Garden. Allah is the patron of believers, tests people, knows their deeds and secret talk, and will not pardon those who die as disbelievers.

l: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: Muhammad is told that there is no Allah save Allah and to ask forgiveness for his sin and for believing men and women. He is also told that he may recognize people by their marks and the burden of their talk.

l: believers, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: Believers follow the truth from their Lord, do good works, and receive removal of their ill-deeds and improvement of their state. They are commanded to help Allah, obey Allah and the messenger, remain steadfast, and spend in the way of Allah.

l: disbelievers, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: Disbelievers follow falsehood, turn people from the way of Allah, oppose the messenger, and hate what Allah has revealed. Their actions are made vain, they face perdition and the Fire, and Allah will not pardon those who die disbelievers.

l: messenger, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: The messenger is to be obeyed, and those who oppose him after guidance has been manifested will not hurt Allah and will have their actions made fruitless.

l: Garden, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: The Garden is promised to those who keep their duty to Allah. It contains rivers of unpolluted water, milk, wine, and clear-run honey, every kind of fruit, and pardon from Allah.

l: Fire, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: The Fire is the habitation of disbelievers. Its inhabitants are immortal and are given boiling water that tears their bowels.

l: way of Allah, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: Those who turn people from the way of Allah or turn away from it have their actions made vain. Allah calls people to spend in the way of Allah and promises help to those who help Allah.

l: revelation, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: The revelation is described as truth from the Lord. Those who are averse to what Allah has revealed have their actions made fruitless, and some people promise to obey those who hate the revelation.

l: Qur'an, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: People are asked whether they will meditate on the Qur'an or whether there are locks on their hearts.

l: battle, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: In battle, believers are instructed to strike those who disbelieve until they are routed, then make captives fast in bonds, followed by grace or ransom until the war lays down its burdens.

l: war, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: When war is mentioned in a decisive surah, those with disease in their hearts look at Muhammad as though fainting unto death. War is to end with grace or ransom after captives are taken.

l: Hour, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: The Hour may come upon people unawares, and its beginnings have already come. When it arrives, warning will no longer benefit those who had not taken heed.

l: actions, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: Allah renders the actions of disbelievers and those who oppose His revelation vain. Believers are warned not to render their own actions vain, and Allah will not grudge the reward of their actions.

l: guidance, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: Those who turn back after guidance has been manifested are seduced by Satan. Those who walk aright receive increased guidance and protection against evil.

l: life of the world, Surah 47: Muhammad, Surah 47: Muhammad (Muhammad)
s: The life of the world is described as only sport and pastime. If people believe and ward off evil, Allah gives them their wages and does not ask for their worldly wealth.

It recounts the allegiance beneath the tree, the withheld conflict in the valley of Mecca, the promised near victory and booty, and the vision of entering the Inviolable Place of Worship. It concludes by describing Muhammad and those with him and affirming Allah’s promise of forgiveness and immense reward for believers who do good works.

l: Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: The unit concerns Allah, His messenger, believers, and the conduct expected among them. Believers are instructed to respect the messenger, verify reports, reconcile parties who fight, avoid ridicule, insults, suspicion, spying, and backbiting, and recognize that people were made into nations and tribes to know one another. It distinguishes true faith from mere submission and describes true believers as those who believe without doubt and strive with their wealth and lives for Allah’s cause. Allah is described as forgiving, merciful, knowing, wise, and aware of what people do.

l: Allah, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: Allah is described as Hearer, Knower, Forgiving, Merciful, Wise, Aware, and Seer of what people do. Allah endears faith to believers, makes disbelief, lewdness, and rebellion hateful to them, loves those who act equitably, and knows the unseen of the heavens and earth.

l: Muhammad, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: Muhammad is addressed as Allah’s messenger and is presented as the one whose presence and voice believers must respect. He is told to say that the wandering Arabs have submitted but do not yet believe, and that their surrender is not a favour to him.

l: believers, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: Believers are told not to be forward before Allah and His messenger, raise their voices above the Prophet’s, or call him from behind the private apartments. They are instructed to verify reports, reconcile fighting parties, avoid ridicule, insults, suspicion, spying, and backbiting, and are described as brothers who should make peace.

l: faith, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: Faith is described as something Allah endears and beautifies in believers’ hearts. True believers believe in Allah and His messenger without doubt and strive with their wealth and lives for Allah’s cause, while submission alone is not yet faith entering the heart.

l: fighting, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: When two parties of believers fall to fighting, others are instructed to make peace between them. If one party wrongs the other, it is to be fought until it returns to Allah’s ordinance, after which peace is to be made justly.

l: peace, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: Peace is to be made between fighting parties and among believing brothers. It is to be established justly and equitably, and Allah loves those who act equitably.

l: suspicion, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: Believers are instructed to shun much suspicion because some suspicion is a crime. They are also told not to spy on one another.

l: backbiting, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: Believers are forbidden to backbite one another. Backbiting is compared to eating the flesh of a dead brother, something they abhor.

l: conduct, Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat), Surah 49: The Inner Apartments (Al-Hujuraat)
s: The unit teaches respectful and equitable conduct, including patience, verification of reports, reconciliation, avoidance of ridicule and insulting nicknames, and recognition that the noblest people in Allah’s sight are those best in conduct.

l: Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf) concerns the Glorious Qur'an, the warning brought by a warner, and the disbelievers' denial and doubt. It describes Allah's creation, knowledge of man, recording of deeds, death, resurrection, judgment, hell, and the Garden. It recalls destroyed peoples and calls Muhammad to bear their words, praise his Lord, and warn by the Qur'an those who fear the threat.

l: Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: It is revealed at Mecca and presents warnings about creation, death, resurrection, judgment, hell, and the Garden.

l: the Glorious Qur'an, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: It is associated with the oath at the opening of the unit and is a means of warning those who fear Allah's threat.

l: Allah, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: Allah created the heavens, the earth, and man, knows what man's soul whispers, records deeds, gives life and death, and will judge and recompense people.

l: Muhammad, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: Muhammad is told to bear what the disbelievers say, praise his Lord, and warn by the Qur'an those who fear Allah's threat. He is not a compeller over them.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: They marvel at the warner, call his message a strange thing, deny the truth, and doubt that the dead will be raised.

l: a warner, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: A warner of the disbelievers' own has come to them.

l: the earth, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: The earth takes part of the dead, is spread out with firm hills, and produces lovely kinds of growth. It will split asunder from the dead when they come forth.

l: the resurrection of the dead, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: It is compared to Allah giving life to a dead land, and the unit affirms that the resurrection will occur.

l: man, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: Man was created by Allah, and Allah knows what his soul whispers to him and is nearer to him than his jugular vein.

l: death, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: The agony of death comes in truth, and the dying person is told that it is what he used to shun.

l: the threatened Day, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: It is the Day for which the trumpet is blown and on which people come forth for judgment.

l: every soul, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: Every soul comes with a driver and a witness.

l: the evil-doer, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: The evil-doer is told that he was heedless, his covering has been removed, and his sight is piercing. He is ordered to be hurled into hell with every rebel ingrate, hinderer of good, transgressor, and doubter.

l: hell, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: Hell is asked whether it is filled and replies that more may come. The evil-doer is commanded to be hurled into its dreadful doom.

l: the Garden, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: The Garden is brought near for those who kept from evil, including every penitent and heedful one who feared the Beneficent in secret and came with a contrite heart.

l: the judgment, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: The judgment includes the sentence that cannot be changed, the questioning of hell, the bringing near of the Garden, and the recompense of people.

l: the (Awful) Cry, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: The (Awful) Cry will be heard in truth on the day of coming forth from the graves.

l: the gathering, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: The gathering occurs when the earth splits asunder from the dead and they hasten forth; it is easy for Allah to make.

l: creation, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: Allah created the heavens and the earth and all between them in six Days, was not touched by weariness, and can create man again.

l: the Day of immortality, Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf), Surah 50: The letter Qaaf (Qaaf)
s: Those who enter the Garden are told to enter in peace, and it is called the day of immortality.

l: Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The unit concerns the certainty of Allah's doom and the day when the heaven heaves and the mountains move. It contrasts deniers, who are thrust into the Fire of hell and punished for what they did, with those who kept their duty, who dwell in gardens and delight. It describes believers whose faithful seed are joined with them and who receive food, drink, spouses, and service. Muhammad is told to warn, wait patiently for his Lord's decree, and hymn Allah's praise, while the deniers' claims and challenges are rejected.

l: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The Mount is named as the first of several things by which Allah swears.

l: Allah, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: Allah is described as the Lord whose doom will surely come to pass and whom the believers pray to as the Benign and Merciful. Muhammad is told to wait patiently for Allah's decree and hymn His praise.

l: Muhammad, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: Muhammad is told to warn people, and the text rejects the claims that he is a soothsayer, madman, or poet. He is told to wait patiently for his Lord's decree and hymn Allah's praise.

l: Scripture, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The Scripture is described as inscribed on fine parchment unrolled.

l: doom of Allah, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The doom of Allah will surely come to pass, and none can ward it off.

l: heaven, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The heaven will heave with an awful heaving, and a fragment of it may fall while the deniers call it a heap of clouds.

l: deniers, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The deniers play in talk of grave matters, deny the Fire, and refuse to believe. They are thrust into the Fire of hell, their guile will not avail them, and they will not be helped.

l: Fire of hell, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The Fire of hell is the torment into which the deniers are thrust. They are told that it is the Fire they used to deny and that enduring or not enduring its heat is the same for them.

l: those who kept their duty, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: Those who kept their duty dwell in gardens and delight, happy because of what their Lord has given them and because He has warded the torment of hell-fire from them.

l: gardens and delight, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: Gardens and delight are the dwelling of those who kept their duty. There they eat and drink in health, recline on ranged couches, and receive other pleasures.

l: believers, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: Believers whose seed follow them in faith have their seed joined to them, without being deprived of anything from their work. They receive desired fruit and meat, cups without vanity or cause of sin, and service from menservants.

l: torment of the breath of Fire, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The torment of the breath of Fire is something from which Allah preserved those who used to pray to Him.

l: speech like the Scripture, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The deniers are challenged to produce speech the like of the Scripture if they are truthful.

l: punishment, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: Those who do wrong have a punishment beyond the punishment of the day when they are thunder-stricken, though most of them do not know.

l: day of thunder-striking, Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur), Surah 52: The Mount (At-Tur)
s: The day of thunder-striking is the day when the deniers meet their appointed day. Their guile will avail them nothing on that day, nor will they be helped.

l: Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: This unit concerns Muhammad, the revelation given to him, and Allah’s signs, power, and judgment. It describes the mighty teacher showing Muhammad the revelation and states that Muhammad’s heart did not lie about what he saw. It rejects the idols and the claims of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter, while affirming that Allah owns the afterlife and the former life. It teaches that each person receives according to human effort and calls people to prostrate themselves before Allah and serve Him.

l: Muhammad, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: Muhammad is described as not erring or speaking from his own desire, and as receiving inspiration. He saw the mighty teacher and greater revelations of his Lord, and he is told to withdraw from those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah.

l: Allah, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: Allah is the source of the revelation, owns whatever is in the heavens and earth, and gives leave for intercession. He rewards those who do evil and those who do good, is aware of people, and is described as the goal, the giver of life and death, the enricher, and the destroyer of earlier peoples.

l: the mighty teacher (Gabriel), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The mighty teacher taught Muhammad and appeared as one vigorous who became clear to view on the uppermost horizon. He drew near to Muhammad until he was two bows’ lengths or nearer.

l: the idols, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The idols Al-Lat, Al-'Uzza, and Manat are described as names given by people and their fathers without any warrant from Allah. The claims made about them follow guesswork and desire.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The disbelievers in the Hereafter name the angels with female names without knowledge. They follow guesswork, and some people turn away from the remembrance of Allah while desiring only the life of the world.

l: the angels, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The angels’ intercession has no effect unless Allah gives permission to whom He chooses and accepts. The disbelievers name the angels with the names of females.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The Hereafter belongs to Allah, and those who disbelieve in it are criticized for their claims about the angels. The threatened Hour is described as near.

l: the life of the world, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The life of the world is desired by those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah. Allah owns both the former life and the afterlife.

l: the guidance, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The guidance from their Lord has come to those who follow guesswork and desire. The unit presents it as a revealed correction to their claims.

l: the Hour, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The threatened Hour is near, and none beside Allah can disclose it.

l: the revelation, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: The revelation is an inspiration given to Muhammad by Allah through the mighty teacher. Muhammad saw one of the greater revelations of his Lord.

l: the remembrance of Allah, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: Some people flee from the remembrance of Allah and desire only the life of the world. Muhammad is told to withdraw from such a person.

l: human effort, Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm), Surah 53: The Star (An-Najm)
s: Man has only that for which he makes effort, and his effort will be seen. He will afterward be repaid for it with fullest payment.

l: Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The Hour, the moon, warnings, and the Qur'an are described in relation to denial, punishment, and remembrance. The folk of Noah, A'ad, Thamud, the folk of Lot, and the house of Pharaoh reject warnings and suffer different punishments, while Noah, Lot, and the family of Lot receive deliverance or help. The guilty are destined for error, madness, and the Fire, whereas the righteous will dwell among gardens and rivers in the favour of a Mighty King.

l: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The Moon is described as having been rent in twain when the Hour drew nigh.

l: the Hour, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The Hour is an appointed tryst that will be more wretched and bitter than earthly failure. On its day, the Summoner summons people to a painful thing, and the dead come forth from their graves.

l: warnings, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: Warnings come to people through news, revelation, and messengers, but many deny them or doubt them. The text repeatedly describes punishment after warnings.

l: the folk of Noah, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The folk of Noah denied and called Noah a madman, and he was repulsed.

l: Noah, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: Noah cried to the Lord after being vanquished and was given help. He was carried upon a thing of planks and nails, and the ark was left as a token.

l: the Lord, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The Lord received Noah's cry and gave him help by opening the gates of heaven and causing the earth to gush forth springs.

l: the ark, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The ark carried Noah upon the waters in the sight of the Lord as a reward for him who was rejected. It was left as a token.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The Qur'an is made easy to remember, but the text asks whether there is anyone who remembers.

l: A'ad, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: A'ad rejected warnings and suffered a raging wind on a day of constant calamity.

l: raging wind, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The raging wind was let loose upon A'ad and swept men away as though they were uprooted trunks of palm-trees.

l: Thamud, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: Thamud rejected warnings and questioned whether they should follow a mortal man among them. They were punished after their comrade hamstrung the she-camel.

l: the she-camel, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The she-camel was sent as a test for Thamud, and its water was to be shared with them. Thamud's comrade took and hamstrung it.

l: the Shout, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The Shout was sent upon Thamud, and they became like dry twigs rejected by the builder of a cattle-fold.

l: the folk of Lot, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The folk of Lot rejected warnings, doubted Lot's warnings, and sought his guests for an ill purpose. They were punished by a storm of stones, except for the family of Lot.

l: Lot, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: Lot warned his folk of the Lord's blow, but they doubted the warnings. The Lord rescued Lot's family in the last watch of the night.

l: the family of Lot, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The family of Lot was rescued from the storm of stones in the last watch of the night as grace from the Lord.

l: the storm of stones, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The storm of stones was sent upon the folk of Lot, except for the family of Lot.

l: the house of Pharaoh, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: Warnings came in truth to the house of Pharaoh, but its people denied the revelations, every one.

l: Pharaoh, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: Pharaoh's house denied the revelations, and the Lord grasped them with the grasp of the Mighty, the Powerful.

l: the guilty, Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar), Surah 54: The Moon (Al-Qamar)
s: The guilty are in error and madness. On the day of doom, they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces.
